editorial:
Imagine waking up and realizing you forgot the most important case of your career, only to find out a man is about to be executed because of your old work. That is the wild ride you get here. You follow Roy Freeman, a former detective who is struggling with a broken memory. He has to go back into the dark files of a ten-year-old murder to see if he made a huge mistake. The whole vibe is moody and tense, making you feel the pressure as the clock ticks down for the guy on death row. It feels like a puzzle where the pieces are missing, and you are trying to solve it right along with the main character.

The acting is top-notch and keeps you glued to the screen, though some parts of the middle feel a bit slow. However, the twists at the end make the wait totally worth it. If you love a good crime mystery that keeps you guessing, you need to see this.
endingExplained: In the end, you discover that Roy did not just forget the case; he was manipulated by people he trusted. The twist reveals that the evidence was planted to frame an innocent man and protect a high-ranking official. Roy finally remembers the truth and manages to provide the proof needed to stop the execution. He clears the man's name and exposes the corruption, proving that some secrets are too dangerous to stay buried.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves gritty detective stories and big plot twists.
